problem_statement:
Provide refresh interval config for GOMEMLIMIT to support dynamic memory limits

### Proposal

The Automatically set `GOMEMLIMIT` to match Linux container or system memory limit functionality currently initializes `GOMEMLIMIT` only once at startup by invoking `memlimit.SetGoMemLimitWithOpts` with `memlimit.WithRatio` as the sole option. Consequently, if the container’s cgroup memory limit changes during runtime, for example, when a Vertical Pod Autoscaler (VPA) updates resource limits, the Go runtime’s `GOMEMLIMIT` remains unchanged and continues to reflect the value determined at startup.

The underlying `automemlimit` library already supports periodically refreshing the memory limit via `WithRefreshInterval`, which could be used to ensure `GOMEMLIMIT` stays synchronized with runtime cgroup memory limit changes.

problem_statement:
Logging inconsistancies when using JSON format

### What did you do?

Standard json level logging. 

Consider the following output
```
{"time":"2025-06-23T15:19:46.651560551Z","level":"INFO","source":"head.go:657","msg":"Replaying on-disk memory mappable chunks if any","component":"tsdb"}
{"time":"2025-06-23T15:19:46.855280406Z","level":"INFO","source":"head.go:744","msg":"On-disk memory mappable chunks replay completed","component":"tsdb","duration":"203.668539ms"}
{"time":"2025-06-23T15:19:46.855333123Z","level":"INFO","source":"head.go:752","msg":"Replaying WAL, this may take a while","component":"tsdb"}
{"time":"2025-06-23T15:19:49.103254671Z","level":"INFO","source":"head.go:789","msg":"WAL checkpoint loaded","component":"tsdb"}
{"time":"2025-06-23T15:19:51.021832221Z","level":"INFO","source":"head.go:825","msg":"WAL segment loaded","component":"tsdb","segment":798,"maxSegment":803,"duration":1918514118}
...
{"time":"2025-06-23T15:19:55.209431089Z","level":"INFO","source":"head.go:825","msg":"WAL segment loaded","component":"tsdb","segment":803,"maxSegment":803,"duration":1577218}
{"time":"2025-06-23T15:19:55.209468194Z","level":"INFO","source":"head.go:862","msg":"WAL replay completed","component":"tsdb","checkpoint_replay_duration":"2.247965902s","wal_replay_duration":"6.106151553s","wbl_replay_duration":"162ns","chunk_snapshot_load_duration":"0s","mmap_chunk_replay_duration":"203.668539ms","total_replay_duration":"8.557856356s"}
```

What is duration? Is it a long integer or a text string? 
If one passes logs off to some standard processing for parsing and storing output logs what type shall we use for duration? Sometimes it a text, sometime a number. Sometime human readable, others not.
It's certainly doesn't lend itself to analysis.


 

### What did you expect to see?

When logging a field, that field should mean the same thing every time it is used, and lend itself to machine read analytics. This should ideally be documented. So duration for example might [always] be a float representing seconds. 

During normal operation live, debug messages should expect to disabled. and only [true] errors, warnings and interactions with external systems, and configuration should be logged. 

### What did you see instead? Under which circumstances?

Further, why log all this as info? I'll warrant to 99% of users a line like
```
{"time":"2025-06-23T15:19:51.021832221Z","level":"INFO","source":"head.go:825","msg":"WAL segment loaded","component":"tsdb","segment":798,"maxSegment":803,"duration":1918514118}
```
means very little. This should better be logged as debug. It's internal to Prometheus ecosystem so make it debug.

```

n/a
```

see above

problem_statement:
tsdb: Close() errors silently discarded in Querier and blockChunkQuerierForRange cleanup

I noticed a couple of cleanup paths in `tsdb/db.go` where errors returned from `Close()` are currently ignored.

This happens in `Querier()` and `blockChunkQuerierForRange()`:

```go
for _, q := range blockQueriers {
    _ = q.Close()
}
```

These cleanup defers run while handling an error path from the surrounding function. If one of the queriers also fails during `Close()`, that information is currently discarded, so the caller only sees the original error.

One possible improvement would be to preserve both errors using `errors.Join()` so the cleanup failure is not lost, for example:

```go
if closeErr := q.Close(); closeErr != nil {
    err = errors.Join(err, fmt.Errorf("close querier during cleanup: %w", closeErr))
}
```

This would keep the original failure while still surfacing any cleanup issues that happen while closing the queriers.
